themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 4.1 per week—a 288% increase with z-score of 6.73—suggesting a sudden deterioration in building systems or public facility upkeep across Crown Heights.
evidence: 16 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (288% spike)
Z-score of 6.73 indicates statistically severe deviation
District has standing budget request for additional building inspectors, suggesting chronic maintenance capacity gaps
reporting_angles: What specific buildings or facilities are generating the spike—NYCHA housing, parks, or commercial?
Are maintenance delays linked to staffing cuts or contractor issues at city agencies?

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% spike with z-score of 5.21—indicating possible issues with sidewalk obstruction, noise, or sanitation tied to restaurant expansion in the district.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 5.21)
Spike coincides with post-holiday/winter season when outdoor dining typically increases
1034-1042 Atlantic Ave FRESH Point 2 development in pipeline may be driving commercial activity
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or blocks are generating complaints—are they new or long-established?
Are complaints focused on noise, sidewalk blockage, or sanitation issues?

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.5 per week—a 220% increase with z-score of 3.67—pointing to emerging public order or quality-of-life issues in the neighborhood.
evidence: 8 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly baseline (220% spike, z-score 3.67)
Safety complaints also spiked 100% TWO WEEKS AGO (15 complaints vs 7.5 baseline), suggesting sustained trend
No corresponding Reddit or local news coverage suggests issue may be under-reported
reporting_angles: What types of non-emergency incidents are driving calls—loitering, quality-of-life crimes, or specific hotspots?
Are there geographic concentrations (e.g., specific subway stations, parks, commercial corridors)?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Vandalism Wave
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 12 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 2.8 per week—a 336% increase with z-score of 4.66—suggesting a coordinated or sustained vandalism campaign in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights.
evidence: 12 graffiti complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.8 weekly baseline (336% increase, z-score 4.66)
Sustained spike suggests pattern rather than isolated incidents
No recent news coverage suggests community awareness may lag actual problem
reporting_angles: Are tags concentrated in specific areas or affecting transit infrastructure, storefronts, or residential buildings?
Is this part of a larger citywide gang or crew activity, or localized to Crown Heights?

themes_detail.label: Flooring & Stair Safety Issues
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stair complaints jumped to 31 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 15.1 per week—a 105% increase with z-score of 4.08—indicating accelerating building code violations and fall hazards in residential or commercial properties.
evidence: 31 flooring/stair complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 15.1 weekly baseline (105% increase, z-score 4.08)
475 building permits filed in past 90 days (283 alterations) suggest active renovation activity that may be causing code violations
District has standing budget request for additional building inspectors, correlating with inspection/enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Are violations concentrated in NYCHA housing, private residential buildings, or commercial spaces?
Are violations linked to unpermitted renovations or deferred maintenance in aging buildings?
